principles: Contract-first: §5 freezes the data shapes + story breakdown so the build can proceed in parallel, mirroring the parallel-decomposition program.
Honest MVP/future split: clearly separate what the MVP builds from not-yet-implemented surfaces; never overclaim.
Compose, do not reinvent: define the capability ON TOP of the existing lattice-review-* lanes + review_run/pass/finding + full-3x2 escalation.
Evidence-grounded + precisely attributed: cite the real S4/S5/B-b29e defects and attribute each to the component (dimensional lens vs completeness critic) that actually found it.
Standalone-readable: define every term (full-3x2, the lens set) inline.
drivers: the spec must let a reader build the capability contract-first
must compose Lattice existing review substrate, not depend on the harness Workflow tool
must be honest about MVP vs future and precisely attribute the empirical evidence

options.name: spec-with-build-program
pros: one design doc that both motivates AND freezes a buildable contract+story breakdown
cons: does not itself build the capability (that is the follow-on B-impl program)

options.name: build-first-no-spec
cons: no frozen contract -> the build churns; the methodology design decisions (data shapes, convergence rule, escalation binding) get made ad hoc; contradicts the contract-first lesson the methodology itself proved

rationale: A design spec that motivates (evidence), specifies (methodology + data shapes), defines the Lattice integration contract (MVP vs future), and freezes the implementation-program breakdown lets the capability be built contract-first — the exact lesson the parallel-decomposition program (and this methodology) proved. Building first without the frozen contract would churn on the very design decisions (convergence rule, escalation-ledger binding, lens/finding/verdict shapes) the spec exists to settle.

preMortem.scenario: The spec overclaims — describes a CLI review mode / escalation tier as if it exists, when only the methodology + a reusable orchestration is realistic for MVP
preMortem.trigger: §4 blurs MVP and future, presenting aspirational surfaces as built
preMortem.consequence: a reader/operator believes a feature exists that does not — the exact dishonesty the methodology is meant to prevent
preMortem.mitigation: §4 has an explicit MVP-vs-future table; every future surface is labeled not-yet-implemented; the deliverable is a SPEC and says so

preMortem.scenario: The empirical evidence is mis-attributed (e.g. crediting the completeness critic for a defect a dimensional lens found), undermining the spec credibility
preMortem.trigger: copying the loose background framing without checking the merged findings
preMortem.consequence: the central motivation is factually wrong; reviewers reject it
preMortem.mitigation: §1 cites each defect with its story id + the EXACT filing component (per the INIT-review correction: S4 crash = quality/crashsafe lens; S5 doors + B-b29e = completeness critic); verifiable against findings.json

preMortem.scenario: The frozen data shapes / story breakdown in §5 are too vague to build from, so the follow-on program cannot proceed contract-first
preMortem.trigger: §5 lists story titles without scopes/deps/acceptance or without concrete lens/finding/verdict schemas
preMortem.consequence: the build still has to design the contract -> the spec failed its one job
preMortem.mitigation: §2/§3 give concrete schemas; §5 gives each build story a scope + dependencies + acceptance, mirroring the parallel-decomposition §8 breakdown
